facts.fact: The document, issued by the Government of Sierra Leone as the National Digital Development Policy 2021, calls its launch a game-changer and states that it succeeds the National ICT Policy 2009 (reviewed 2016/2017); it also recommends that the policy be approved, and gives no adoption date beyond 2021.

The full text is hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation website (mocti.gov.sl); the document gives no date of its own beyond 2021 on its cover, so the published date is used.
The policy states no end year for itself and says it shall be reviewed every five years; the 2039 middle-income goal it names is a national aim, not its period.

The policy contains no costed or dated action plan: it recommends that the ministry develop an implementation plan, and says a National Digital Development Strategy will set targets, sub-plans and resources.

The policy reports no progress against itself; it recommends that the ministry develop a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework and says an M&E system on agreed sector indicators shall be built, with a review every five years.

The policy gives the Ministry of Information and Communications, through its Directorate of Communications, the role of monitoring, evaluating and reviewing the policy's implementation, and proposes a National Digital Development Agency and Council to coordinate it.

The policy states no budget line for itself: it lists as objectives allocating a proportion of the national budget to e-government and a Partners Coordinating Committee to analyse financing gaps, and names the Digital Impact Alliance of the United Nations Foundation as giving financial and technical support to its development.
